, in this paper, we present a distributed, dynamic time slot allocation scheme for dynamically establishing and terminating real-time message streams, with message temporal guarantees, in single-hop WDM star-coupled networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by exploiting the time slot structure of the data channels in the star-coupled architecture, the proposed dynamic time slot allocation scheme is able to efficiently establish/terminate message streams in response the call requests.

, by decomposing a message stream into a number of message sub-stream, the problem of allocating time slots on the shared W data channels to the message stream can be reduced to that of allocating time slots to the message sub-streams.

the proposed dynamic slot assignment scheme, with its distributed nature, is able to dynamically establish and release isochronous streams on demand, and is able to adapt to changes in the message arrival rates, and in the number of active stations, without the need for global knowledge.
